meta.topic: Why your Python projects keep breaking - packages, dependencies, and the one folder nobody makes
meta.onePayoff: You will know exactly what breaks a working Python project, why nothing crashes when it happens, and the shape of the fix.
meta.openLoop: Two projects on one laptop. You install something for the first, and the second one breaks - without you touching a single character of it.
meta.analogy: THE SHELF - packages are labelled parcels, your machine has one shelf, and every project reaches into the same shelf. Drawn as objects, established out loud before it is used (LAW 0l).
meta.artefacts: briefs/uv/research/04-pip-transcripts.md - every terminal frame in this chapter is a real capture
meta.designNote: terminalcli pack, STILL background (LAW 0h). PLAN.md rule: the second pane is NEVER a list of lit text rows. Several of these beats want ONE full-bleed picture, not a split.

beats.intent: COLD OPEN, no branding. A program that worked yesterday, run again today, and Python says it cannot find a module the viewer knows they installed. Show the real traceback as a real terminal, and the confusion on the word 'installed'.
beats.ideal: A terminal that runs, fails, and leaves the error sitting there. Not a card about errors.

beats.intent: Name the promise the title made: by the end you will know what actually broke, and why nobody warned you. This is where the greeting is woven in as an aside, never announced.
beats.ideal: Title card - the OUTCOME, not the subject.

beats.intent: OPEN THE LOOP and refuse to close it: two projects on one laptop, you install something for the first, and the second breaks although you never opened it. Pose it as a question and move on.
beats.ideal: Two project folders side by side, a hand touching only one, and the other going dark. No text explaining it.

beats.intent: ESTABLISH THE PICTURE OUT LOUD before using it: 'Picture a shelf.' What a package actually is - code somebody else already wrote, that you download and use. Draw the parcel with a printed label: a name and a version number.
beats.ideal: PARCEL_LABEL - a sealed parcel, the label readable, the VERSION being the part that changes.

beats.intent: Where the parcels come from: one enormous public warehouse that anybody can publish to. Name PyPI once, plainly, and show its scale rather than stating it.
beats.ideal: The index as a physical warehouse the parcel is pulled from - a real place, not a cloud icon.

beats.intent: Install one package for real. Type the command, watch it land on the shelf. Everything is fine and the viewer should feel that it is fine.
beats.artefact: pip install rich - first two lines
beats.ideal: The parcel travelling warehouse to shelf, and the shelf now holding one thing.

beats.intent: THE FIRST SURPRISE: you asked for one parcel and four arrived. Read the real output line by line - each extra package, and the CONSTRAINT printed beside it that dragged it in. Define the word dependency here, in its own sentence, with the picture already on screen.
beats.artefact: the full pip install rich transcript, including 'Collecting pygments<3.0.0,>=2.13.0'
beats.ideal: DEPENDENCY_UNFOLD - the parcel opens, a note inside lists more parcels, and those arrive too. One of them was requested by another parcel, not by rich - show that second level.

beats.intent: SILENT BEAT, no narration. The four packages sitting on the shelf, and the order pip installed them in - the deepest one first, the one you asked for last. Let the viewer read it.
beats.ideal: Hold on the real 'Installing collected packages' line. 2-3s. Nothing moves.

beats.intent: Now the part nobody mentions: there is only ONE shelf. Every project on this machine reaches into the same one. Show two different projects, two different jobs, one shared shelf between them.
beats.ideal: SHELF_CLASH, phase one - two projects, one shelf, both reaching. The reaching is the animation.

beats.intent: Each project wants a different version of the SAME parcel. Not different parcels - the same one, at two numbers. Put both demands on screen at once so the impossibility is visible before it is explained.
beats.ideal: One slot on the shelf, two labels competing for it. The slot can hold one.

beats.intent: THE COLLISION, in the tool's own words. Run the install and read pip narrating the overwrite: attempting uninstall, found existing, uninstalling, successfully uninstalled. The incumbent is evicted and nobody asked the project that depended on it.
beats.artefact: the pygments==2.0.0 transcript, the uninstall block
beats.ideal: SHELF_CLASH, phase two - the old label physically lifted out and the new one dropped in. This ANSWERS the loop opened in s03.

beats.intent: THE TWO LINES. pip says ERROR and names the incompatibility - and then, two lines later, says Successfully installed. Put both on screen together and stop talking.
beats.artefact: the ERROR line and the 'Successfully installed pygments-2.0' line, adjacent
beats.ideal: Full-bleed, no split. Two real lines of terminal output, the contradiction between them being the entire beat.

beats.intent: And then - nothing happens. Run the broken thing. It works. Explain honestly that there is no crash, no red text, no moment of discovery: the environment is simply wrong now, and will stay wrong until some other day trips over it. This is why it costs an afternoon.
beats.artefact: rich still printing 'hello' after the break
beats.ideal: The shelf visibly wrong while the program visibly runs. Both true at once - that contradiction is the picture.

beats.intent: The readout that would have told you, and that nobody runs. One command, one plain sentence naming the conflict.
beats.ideal: A health readout on the shelf itself, one row failing.

beats.intent: Name the second failure mode too, the loud one from the cold open: the package is real, it just lives on a different shelf than the one now running. Connect it back to s01 so the viewer knows both errors have the same root.
beats.ideal: Two shelves, the program pointed at the wrong one, the parcel sitting on the other.

beats.intent: QUIZ, with a real thinking gap (LAW 0e-q). You install one package and four arrive - what do we call the three you did not ask for? Ask, invite them to pause, then Ready, then the answer with the why.
beats.ideal: QUIZ_CARD. Question, pause invitation of about four seconds that gives nothing away, then the reveal anchored on 'Ready'.

beats.intent: THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, arrived at as a question the viewer is now holding: what if each project had its own shelf? Show the walls going up between them and both projects working at once with different versions.
beats.ideal: The single shelf splitting into two walled shelves, the same two versions now coexisting. The wall going up IS the idea.

beats.intent: Name it plainly and without ceremony - a folder of packages that belongs to one project. Say the words virtual environment once, then immediately go back to plain language.
beats.ideal: The wall labelled, the folder shown as a folder.

beats.intent: So why does almost nobody do it? The ritual: make it, turn it on, remember which one you are in, turn it off, forget, and be back where you started. Show the ceremony as the obstacle it is - this is the honest reason, not laziness.
beats.ideal: The steps as a physical sequence you must perform every single time, with the forgetting drawn.

beats.intent: CLOSE THE LOOP and name uv for the first time in the whole chapter. One command, and the folder is created, used and forgotten on your behalf - you never think about any of this again. Do not demo it yet; that is the next chapter.
beats.ideal: The whole ceremony from s19 collapsing into a single line. The collapse is the animation.

beats.intent: RECAP that pays off what was promised: the two ways a project breaks, why neither announces itself, and the one idea that removes both.
beats.ideal: RECAP furniture, tied to the objects already established - not new pictures.

beats.intent: Outro: what the next chapter answers - installing uv, and why a tool that installs Python cannot itself be written in Python.
beats.ideal: OUTRO_CTA, centred, end-screen safe.
